title: Paintings after Ancient Masters: A Lady
medium: album leaf, ink and color on silk

image.credit: Cleveland Museum of Art, John L. Severance Fund

phase.label: Late albums, after the fall of the Ming

source.label: CMA: this album is among “the other albums from the latter part of his career”
Sirén: some of Chen’s ladies “[are] actually copied after originals by Chou Fang”

highlight.text: People who saw his paintings said: ‘Your copies surpass the originals; why do you keep on making copies?’ To [which] he answered: ‘That is just where I fall short; the merits of my pictures [are] easily seen, and so [I] have not attained supreme skill. Chou Fang’s [skill] is [consummate]; yet he appears to possess no skill. This is what is really difficult.’
highlight.lead: After copying a Tang picture of ladies by Zhou Fang:

source.title: Reply recorded by Zhang Geng

work.text: It also has one leaf featuring a woman, an often-used subject not found in the other albums from the latter part of his career.
work.lead: The Cleveland Museum, on the album this leaf comes from:

source.author: Cleveland Museum of Art
source.title: Paintings after Ancient Masters: A Lady

work.text: The majority of [Chen Hongshou's] figure-paintings [are] of minor size, on short handscrolls or album-leaves, representing queer and ugly old men (often humorously characterized), or puppet-like young ladies dressed in T'ang fashion. Some of these [are] actually copied after originals by Chou Fang or other famous painters of female [beauties].

source.author: Osvald Sirén
source.title: Chinese Painting: Leading Masters and Principles, vol. V

moment.text: He was very famous at that time, called "Chen in South and Cui in North", together with Cui Zizhong.

matters.text: His fame as a painter, [calligrapher], and poet soon became widespread, as did also his reputation for freedom [with] wine and women.

source.author: Fang Chao-ying
source.title: Ch‘ên Hung-shou
source.publisher: in Arthur W. Hummel (ed.), Eminent Chinese of the Ch‘ing Period, vol. I, US Government Printing Office (Internet Archive scan)
